statement: A CPU has to run a list of tasks. Each task is labelled with its type, given here as an integer from 0 to 25 (standing for the letters A to Z), and every task takes one time unit. In each time unit the CPU either runs one task or stays idle, and tasks may run in any order.

There is a cooldown: two tasks of the same type must be separated by at least n time units, so after running a task of some type at time t, the next task of that type can run no earlier than time t + n + 1.
You are given the array tasks and the integer n. Return the smallest number of time units, idle units included, needed to finish every task.

examples.explanation: One best order is 0, 1, idle, 0, 1, idle, 0, 1. Each type needs two units between its runs, and only two types exist, so two idle units are unavoidable: 8 in total.
Type 0 occurs 5 times, which forces at least (5 − 1) × 3 + 1 = 13 units. There are 14 tasks, though, and enough other types to fill every gap, so no idling is needed and the answer is 14.
With no cooldown, tasks can run back to back, so the 6 tasks take exactly 6 units.
